name: pi Assistant

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created, edited] # edited: a box ticked on one of pi's questions
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]

# The job acts with a GitHub App token, which (unlike GITHUB_TOKEN) triggers workflows: CI on pi's PRs,
# release.yml on its tags. GITHUB_TOKEN itself is not used.
permissions: {}

jobs:
  pi-response:
    # @pi requests, /answer replies, and edits of pi's questions (not other edited comments). Never events
    # from a bot: with an App token, pi's own comments and edits would otherwise start new runs.
    if: >-
      github.event.sender.type != 'Bot'
      && ((github.event.action == 'edited' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '<!-- pi-action:question'))
      || (github.event.action != 'edited' && (contains(github.event.comment.body || github.event.issue.body || github.event.pull_request.body || '', '@pi')
      || contains(github.event.comment.body || '', '/answer'))))
    # Job-level, so runs the `if` skips never take the thread's single pending slot from a real one.
    concurrency:
      group: pi-action-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45

    steps:
      - name: Mint a GitHub App token
        id: app
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.PI_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.PI_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write
          permission-issues: write
          permission-pull-requests: write
          permission-discussions: write
          permission-actions: read
          permission-checks: read
          permission-statuses: read

      - name: Commit as the App's bot user
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
          SLUG: ${{ steps.app.outputs.app-slug }}
        run: |
          id=$(gh api "/users/${SLUG}%5Bbot%5D" --jq .id)
          {
            echo "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=${SLUG}[bot]"
            echo "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=${SLUG}[bot]"
            echo "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=${id}+${SLUG}[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
            echo "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=${id}+${SLUG}[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }} # pushes (branches, tags, refs/pi/threads/*) as the App
          fetch-depth: 0 # tags and history, for release notes and version bumps

      - name: Run pi-action
        uses: cv/pi-action@9a1ef5509660c68074ade266675f4290de5df3a9 # v2.2.0
        with:
          github_token: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
          provider: nvidia
          model: aws/anthropic/bedrock-claude-opus-5-5
          api_key: ${{ secrets.NVIDIA_API_KEY }}
          provider_base_url: https://inference-api.nvidia.com
          provider_api: anthropic-messages
          model_name: Opus 5.5
          model_reasoning: true
          model_input: text,image
          model_context_window: 1050000
          model_max_tokens: 128000 # Bedrock's maximum for Opus 5.5
          compat_force_adaptive_thinking: true
          # A released pit, not this checkout: pi edits the checkout, and its tools shouldn't change under it.
          extensions: github:cv/pit#v0.35.0
# Pit agent workflow

## Edits

Pit's tool description covers fresh anchors and re-reading after edits. In this repository also:

- Prefer `workspace.search` for a single edit target and `workspace.batch` for independent multi-file reads.
- Put multiline, regex-heavy, or quote-heavy patch content in top-level `params` on the first attempt.
- After two failures of the same class, split the operation instead of varying the same construction.

## Tool selection

- Use `npm.test()` for the normal suite and `npm.run(script)` for `check`, `coverage`, and `package:check`.
- Use `shell.execFile("npx", ...)` only for targeted executable invocations without a typed capability.
- Use typed Git and GitHub methods whenever supported. One unsupported GitHub step does not justify raw `gh` for supported view/list/comment/close/run steps.
- Use `shell.exec` only when shell syntax is required.

## Parallelism and ordering

- Keep Git mutations and dependent state transitions sequential.
- Do not run the full test and coverage suites concurrently.
- Format only files changed by the task; never run a broad fixer with unrelated modifications.

## Testing

- Load [pit-test-audit](.pi/skills/pit-test-audit/SKILL.md) before writing, changing, reviewing, or auditing tests. Apply its authoring gate; keep audit discovery read-only until candidate evidence is recorded.

- Prefer typed `it.each` tables when cases share setup and assertion shape but vary inputs and expected outputs.
- Give table rows descriptive names; keep lifecycle, concurrency, ordering, and heterogeneous workflows as explicit standalone tests.
- Do not move substantial control flow into table data merely to reduce line count.

- Prefer observable outcomes and effects over implementation tokens, copied prose, private object identity, or incidental call order. Keep exact assertions for meaningful public contracts and safety boundaries; pit-test-audit's retention bar lists them.

## Terminal UX

- Load the [pit-terminal-ux](.pi/skills/pit-terminal-ux/SKILL.md) skill when designing, implementing, or reviewing custom renderers, tool calls/results, progress, errors, or changes to their supporting data contracts.
- Treat faithful inputs/output, consistent semantic outcomes, explicit omissions, and readable error causes as correctness requirements, not optional polish.
- Review representative collapsed, expanded, partial, and final views at realistic terminal widths. Headless tests do not replace live Pi acceptance for behavior changes.

## Delivery

- Load the `pit-delivery` skill for issue implementation and finalization.
- Run `delivery.validate()` for the standard gates and `delivery.prepare()` before delivery.
- For TUI, extension-loading, saved-function, sandbox, or partial-update changes: push a non-closing commit, reload Pi, and smoke-test before closing the issue.
- Do not use `Closes #...` until interactive acceptance has passed.
